messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Female workers with serum vitamin D below 10 ng/mL had higher odds of depressive symptoms (CES-D 16 or above) than those with higher levels.
Sentence: "The odds ratio of the depressive symptom group with a CES-D score of 16 or above being in the deficiency group with a serum vitamin D level less than 10 ng/mL was found to be 1.55 (95 % CI = 1.15-2.07)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (CES-D score of 16 or above)
Population: 1054 Korean female workers in the manufacturing industry undergoing physical examinations
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (deficiency below 10 ng/mL), measured, not given
Comparator: Serum vitamin D 10 ng/mL or higher
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,054
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational associations of measured vitamin D with depression, but the labels differ (benefit vs harm) with Study B's direction unstated; they differ mainly in population (healthy female workers vs post-COVID inpatients) and cutoffs/instruments.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure","design_or_bias"],"detail":"population: 1,054 Korean female factory workers vs 72 post-COVID hospital patients; PHQ-9 >5 vs CES-D >=16; direction in Study B not stated"}
